```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(avesperu)
```

This vignette shows how to add current Peru-checklist information to a small set of field observations while preserving the submitted names for review.

## Requirements

The examples use only data bundled with `avesperu`.

## Validate a field list

```{r}
field_data <- data.frame(observer = c("Observer A", "Observer B", "Observer A", "Observer C"), species = c("Amazilia amazilia", "Phaetornis guy", "Metallura tyrianthina", "Tangara chilensis"), count = c(2, 1, 3, 5))
details <- search_avesperu(field_data$species, return_details = TRUE)
field_data$accepted_name <- details$accepted_name
field_data$status <- details$status
field_data$family <- details$family_name
field_data
```

Expected result: each submitted name remains associated with its accepted name, status, and family. Rows without an accepted name need manual review.

## Identify endemic species

```{r}
my_species <- c("Penelope albipennis", "Xenoglaux loweryi", "Falco sparverius")
results <- search_avesperu(my_species, return_details = TRUE)
results[results$status == "Endémico", c("accepted_name", "english_name", "family_name")]
```

This pattern is useful for filtering a submitted list, not for replacing a project-specific definition of endemism.

## Review uncertain results

Qualified and hybrid inputs, as well as tied candidates, are retained for review. Detailed output includes audit attributes that describe reconciliation, execution, and the checklist reference.

```{r audit-example}
result <- search_avesperu("Falco CF. sparverius", return_details = TRUE)
attr(result, "reconciliation")
attr(result, "execution")
attr(result, "reference")
```

## Next steps

Use [approximate matching](https://paulesantos.github.io/avesperu/articles/coincidencia-aproximada.html) for spelling variants, or inspect the [reference documentation](https://paulesantos.github.io/avesperu/reference/index.html) for complete function arguments.
